26187.description:
Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Open to PNG national candidates only
Fixed term contract up to three years
About Palladium
Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social, climate and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to help solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, the environment, and, most importantly, people's lives.
About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)
The Papua New Guinea (PNG)–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) program is a new Australian Government investment that will be working in partnership with PNG to strengthen its technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program will work closely with TVET stakeholders and select technical colleges to grow the number of skilled individuals with industry relevant skills.
This Opportunity
As
Procurement Manager
you will be responsible for leading on all procurement activities for the program, ensuring it is conducted in accordance with company and client compliance requirements and is delivered with considerations towards value-for-money, localisation and other program and government objectives.
This will include:
Planning, directing and coordinating all procurement activities in compliance with the
Australian Commonwealth Procurement Rules (CPR’s)
, DFAT
Value for Money
principles, and Palladium procurement and due diligence standards.
Advising management on procurement strategies and sourcing options. Managing the full procurement cycle, including planning, market engagement, solicitation, evaluation, contracting and mobilisation. Procurement may range from simple three quote evaluations to complex competitive tender processes, requiring in-depth preparation and evaluation.
Integrating social procurement principles into all sourcing activities by prioritising suppliers that deliver measurable social, economic and environmental benefits to local businesses, women, youth owned enterprises, people with disability and marginalised groups
Developing and maintaining procurement plans, schedules and templates, and ensuring all procurement documentation—including due diligence records, vendor/contractor files, contract registers and tracking tools—is complete, accurate, auditable, up to date, and fully compliant with DFAT and Palladium requirements.
Reviewing procurement requests to ensure clarity, accuracy, and alignment with SWLT objectives, and support specification and scope development.
Preparing bidding documents (RFQs, RFPs) and leading tender evaluations to ensure transparent bid analysis. Negotiating contracts, pricing and terms with suppliers.
Managing vendor performance to support high‑quality delivery and value‑for‑money outcomes and maintain an up‑to‑date vendor database with performance tracking and quality assurance.
Providing regular reports on procurement progress, risks, timelines and delivery status, including up-to-date strategic advice to senior management.
Developing and maintaining an approved supplier database. Conducting supplier performance evaluations.
Identifying and mitigating procurement risks, escalating critical issues—including conflicts of interest, integrity concerns or suspected fraud—as required, and promote ethical, transparent procurement practices across all SWLT teams and partners.
Understanding and contributing to SWLT gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) objectives as relevant to this role and participate in GEDSI learning and engagement as required.
Adhering to DFAT and Palladium safeguarding standards and policies and commit to prevent harm, and commit to promoting safe, inclusive environments, including reporting concerns appropriately.
Championing ethical procurement practices across all SWLT teams and partners.
Modelling, contributing to and supporting an office culture of learning and performance with colleagues, junior staff and counterparts, building procurement capability across the SWLT team through coaching, guidance and practical support.
Supporting and upholding the organisation’s commitment to environmental sustainability, such as integrating environmental sustainability considerations into procurement decisions, including climate‑friendly options and reduced resource use.
Contributing to the implementation of solutions that deliver value and ensure SWLT principles
[1]
are embedded within program delivery.
About you
You will have experience in:
Procurement in PNG, ideally within DFAT‑funded or donor‑funded development programs
A strong understanding of the Commonwealth Procurement Rules, DFAT procurement requirements and PNG Government procurement processes.
Managing full procurement cycles including complex tenders.
Using strong analytical thinking and proactive problem solving.
Working with suppliers and stakeholders across PNG, including provincial contexts.
An understanding of tertiary and vocational education and training development in the Pacific Islands context is desirable.
Excellent organisational and computer skills especially with MS Word and Excel.
Operate with high levels of integrity, consistent with the intent of
DFAT’s Ethics, Integrity and Professional Standards Policy Manual.
Demonstrated ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively within a team.
Participation and positive engagement in diverse teams, supporting a results-driven culture of learning and inclusion.
Demonstrated commitment to the principles of locally-led, socially inclusive, politically informed and adaptive programming.
To Apply
Please submit your application online, including your CV and brief cover letter, outlining your suitability in line with the requirements of the position via
https://palladium.csod.com/ux/ats/careersite/2/home/requisition/24902?c=palladium&referralToken=_WbZuulmjEWkhAkMjzcBPg
Closing date:
Wednesday 4
th
March 2026, 11.59pm
Equity, Diversity & Inclusion -
Palladium is committed to embedding equity, diversity, and inclusion into everything we do. We welcome applications from all sections of society and actively encourage diversity to drive innovation, creativity, success and good practice. We positively welcome and seek to ensure we achieve diversity in our workforce; and that all job applicants and employees receive equal and fair treatment regardless of their background or personal characteristics. These include: (but are not limited to) socio-economic background, age, race, gender identity and expression, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, nationality, veteran, marital or Indigenous status.
Should you require any adjustments to be made due to a disability or you are a neurodivergent individual or for any other circumstance, please email our team at
[email protected]
and we will be in touch to discuss.
Safeguarding -
We define Safeguarding as “the preventative action taken by Palladium to protect our people, clients and the communities we work with from harm”. We are committed to ensuring that all children and adults who come into contact with Palladium are treated with respect and are free from abuse. All successful candidates will be subject to an enhanced selection process including safeguarding-focused interviews and a rigorous due diligence process.
Apply

Title: SWEEP TB Senior Project Officer    Classification: Ful
l-Time | Contract Level 6
Location: Daru Office (Daru General Hospital), Western Province, Papua New Guinea
Position Snapshot
The Senior Project Officer will work closely with the Project Manager – Western Province Projects and the Team Leader – Technical (TB Working Group), alongside finance, administration and in-country teams, to provide high-level logistical, administrative and operational support across a range of tuberculosis (TB) projects in Western Province, PNG.
This role is ideal for a development or public health professional who thrives in a dynamic environment and enjoys coordinating complex projects with multiple stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities
1. Project Management Support & Coordination
Collect, collate and format project reports, briefs and deliverables.
Support monthly data collection and tracking in collaboration with the TB Specialist – M&E.
Assist in qualitative data analysis (e.g., pre- and post-training evaluations).
Coordinate workshops, meetings, conferences and project activities.
Prepare meeting minutes and track action items.
Maintain project tracking tools and templates.
Ensure compliance with Burnet policies and donor requirements.
Lead travel coordination for consultants and staff (flights, accommodation, visas, registrations, insurance, medical checks, security briefings).
Support GEDSI Community of Practice and Disability Inclusion initiatives in Western Province.
2. Finance Support & Budget Management
Support monthly budget reviews (budget vs actuals).
Assist with transaction coding and financial tracking.
Support detailed costings for new initiatives.
Process payments and reimbursements in liaison with PNG and Melbourne finance teams.
Support procurement and asset register maintenance.
Provide budget oversight during Project Manager leave periods (RID-TB budget).
3. People & HR Coordination
Coordinate recruitment, mobilisation and demobilisation processes for in-country staff.
Support onboarding and orientation of new staff.
Liaise with HR teams in PNG and Melbourne.
Build strong working relationships with country offices and technical teams.
4. Organisational & Administrative Support
Support ANCP reaccreditation documentation collation.
Assist migration and management of Office 365 filing systems.
Provide general administrative support to Project Managers.
Participate in staff meetings, performance reviews and professional development activities.
Act as focal person for ISOS travel training and Office 365 migration support.
Selection Criteria
Essential
Qualification in International Development, Public Health or related field, or 2–5 years equivalent experience.
Demonstrated experience supporting complex projects or programs.
Experience in monitoring & evaluation and donor reporting.
Strong understanding of project-related finance (budgeting, forecasting, procurement, payments).
Experience coordinating travel and visa arrangements.
Highly developed organisational and time management skills.
Strong judgement and problem-solving skills.
Excellent interpersonal and cross-cultural communication skills.
Desirable
Experience in international development/NGO settings.
Experience in qualitative and/or quantitative data collection and analysis.
Experience in public health research.
Occupational Health and Safety
Burnet Institute has a commitment to providing a safe and healthy workplace in accordance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004. All staff are obliged to take all reasonable care to ensure that their actions do not place themselves or others at risk.
Other Requirements
Burnet Institute is a child safe organisation. The incumbent of this position will be required to undergo a Police Check and possibly a Working with Children Check as a condition of employment.
Contact with children:
No Contact With Children
How to Apply
Interested applicants should submit:
A cover letter addressing the key selection criteria, a current CV and contact details of at least two referees.
Applications close:
4
th March 2026
Burnet Institute is committed to child safety, gender equality, disability inclusion, and cultural diversity. We encourage applications from suitably qualified Papua New Guinean nationals and women candidates.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

26236.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Officer Emergency Response will coordinate the preparation, execution, and improvement of emergency response plans and procedures including emergency drills and compliance.
Essential Duties
Support in the preparation and execution of emergency response plans and procedures, ensuring alignment with site-specific needs and regulatory requirements.
Provides coordination and technical guidance to Voluntary ERT members.
Perform regular inspections and maintenance checks of emergency response equipment.
Engage in emergency drills and simulations, helping to prepare and conduct these exercises and deliver feedback for continuous improvement
Provides coordination and guidance for ERT training activities.
Training & Experience

26189.description:
Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Open to PNG national candidates only
Fixed term contract up to two years
About Palladium
Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social, climate and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to help solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, the environment, and, most importantly, people's lives.
About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)
The Papua New Guinea (PNG)–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) program is a new Australian Government investment that will be working in partnership with PNG to strengthen its technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program will work closely with TVET stakeholders and select technical colleges to grow the number of skilled individuals with industry relevant skills.
This Opportunity
As
Senior Project Coordinator
you will be responsible for providing cross pillar support to manage the implementation and delivery of a range of SWLT activities under the direction of the senior leadership team and in-consultation with technical advisers and partners.
You will provide flexible and adaptive project management support to technical leads across policy reform and advisory activities across the TVET and skills system. Activities will cover a diverse portfolio of technical assistance including grants, infrastructure, organisational capacity assessments, labour market analysis, gender and inclusion work, safeguards and sector coordination activities.
The Senior Project Coordinator will work under an agile reporting framework and will report to different technical leads or members of the senior leadership team at different times, depending on activity requirements.
This will include:
Support technical leads in engagement with Government of PNG counterparts, DFAT, technical partners and consultants to support activity design, consultation, and delivery.
Lead and support the preparation of Concept Notes, Terms of Reference, briefing papers, draft deliverables and other outputs from early scoping through drafting, review, approval, and completion.
Lead and maintain program trackers, delivery schedules, and workplans to support effective decision-making.
Identify delivery risks and bottlenecks across activities and proactively support mitigation actions with technical leads.
Monitor alignment between approved budgets, scopes of work, and delivery progress across multiple activities.
Support preparation and follow-up for steering committees, technical advisory groups, coordination forums, workshops, and consultations.
Work with the operations focal points including SWLT Procurement and Finance Managers on activity procurement processes including scoping, scheduling and documentation.
Assist the technical leads and Operations Senior Coordinator with managing consultants and partners, including contract milestones, deliverable tracking, and reporting requirements.
Contribute to monitoring and reporting against program outputs, priorities, and agreed indicators, including dashboard and tracker inputs as required.
Provide responsive, ad‑hoc program management and coordination support as priorities shift, new requests emerge, or activities are brought forward or deferred.
Understand and contribute to SWLT gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) objectives as relevant to this role and participate in GEDSI learning and engagement as required.
Ensure adherence to DFAT and Palladium safeguarding standards and policies and commit to prevent harm, and commit to promoting safe, inclusive environments, including reporting concerns appropriately.
Contribute to office learning culture by seeking out knowledge, sharing fresh perspectives and ideas, and taking initiative in problem-solving.
Support SWLT to be climate friendly by thinking about and implementing ways to reduce waste and use environmental practices.
Understand and work in line with SWLT principles at all times.
About you
You will have demonstrated experience in:
Strong program management skills with the ability to coordinate multiple activities at the same time and at different stages, and with varying stakeholders
Proven ability to manage complex workplans and trackers that maintain oversight of activity performance.
Demonstrated interpersonal skills to work effectively with internal and external stakeholders and act as a trusted coordination point across diverse audiences
Demonstrated understanding of MEL tools underpinning results monitoring frameworks
A practical understanding of procurement processes and financial management, including an ability to understand and analyse activity budgets
Capacity to support adaptive management, responding to shifting priorities and changes in direction
Strong skills in writing, reviewing, and being able to interpret and synthesise information readily
High level of organisation, initiative and self-management and the ability to work across priority tasks and adhoc requests while also working collaboratively with senior, technical staff and driving progress
Participation and positive engagement in diverse teams, supporting a results-driven culture of learning and inclusion
Demonstrated commitment to the principles of locally-led, socially inclusive, politically informed and adaptive programming.
Please note:
This role is being advertised early in the program’s inception phase. Some aspects of the role may be revised before or shortly after commencement. Any changes will be discussed and agreed upon between Palladium and the successful candidate.

Camps Superintendent
Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our Simberi Operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking a
Camps Superintendent
to join our team on a Fixed-Term (One-Year) position at our Simberi Operations. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 21/14 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Buka, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Wewak, Vanimo, or Tabar group of Islands.
(
Locals are encouraged to apply)
.
Reporting to the Manager Commercial, the Camps Superintendent manages all camp services; accommodation, catering, laundry, maintenance, logistics and staff, ensuring safety, quality, and cost-efficiency in a remote setting. Key duties involve budgeting, procurement, staff supervision, maintenance oversight, and meeting service level agreements (SLAs) for a productive mining workforce.
The opportunity

Operations Management: Oversee daily camp operations (accommodation, Catering, laundry, water/power), coordinate logistics (transport, arrivals/departures), and manage maintenance/upgrades.

Are you ready to come and build your future with us?
We need the best people. People who have the drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​

26085.description:
LANDS OFFICER
Hargy Oil Palms Limited (HOPL) is an Oil Palm plantation company based in Bialla, West New Britain Province. A remote location situated approximately 2 and half hours’ drive east of Kimbe town.
HOPL currently has a vacancy for a suitably qualified and experienced Lands Officer who will join its General Administration Department and deliver support services to HOPL, its Oil Palm Growers and stakeholders.
Primary Objectives:
Reporting to the Lands Manager, the Lands Officer will be required to provide support to the Small Holder Oil Palm growers and facilitate the dissemination of land instruments related to the acquisition and granting of state leases and where possible assist in the processing of land applications for Oil palm land settlement schemes and Village Oil Palm blocks. The role will also be required to assist in the maintenance and registration of any Oil Palm extension projects for the HOPL and ensure that all statutory requirements are fully ascertained for the company under the RSPO, free, prior informed consent process.
Competencies
To perform the job successfully, it is expected that the applicant can demonstrate the following competencies:
Arrange community engagement message tracks for Free, Prior and Informed consent for land acquisition expansion projects.
Assist in the facilitation and formation of ILGs to ensure that all have proper constitutions and work closely with the district commerce officers to establishing solid business practices for the registered groups.
To facilitate the process of registration of all Lease-Leaseback land dealings involving ILGs desirable in new Oil Palm development projects and guide them on the rights and obligations conversant with the laws of PNG.
Able to assist in the delivery of alternate dispute resolution mechanism approaches where there is dispute over ownership of land with the support from the relevant government agencies.
Work with Smallholder Extension services officers and the OPIC to ensure that Clan Land Use Agreements (CLUA for all Village Oil Palm blocks are appropriately registered using the FPIC process.
Assist in the preparation and delivery of awareness on important land matters to the Bialla Smallholder Oil Palm growers.
Be responsible for the lodgement of all land title instruments at the National Department of Lands, the WNB Provincial Lands Division and other relevant government authorities.
Follow up with Provincial lands division and the National Department of lands and other relevant authorities to ensure that documentation related to the granting of state leases and any land applications are processed in a timely manner.
Review and implement Standard Operating Procedures for the land payment system, Lease-Leaseback and other internal land administrative matters.
Technical knowledge on the use of a hand-held GPS in undertaking GPS surveys to identify land boundaries and any conflicting or overlapping areas.
Willing to live and work in a remote area or setting.
Any other relevant duties as required.
Education and Background
Degree in Land Studies or related with 2-5 years of job experience in a similar role.
Experience in ADR techniques, deep understanding of clan structures and the social norms of West New Britain Province.
Some experience in the formulation of message tracks, delivery of community engagement consultations in public meetings, and public speaking.
Knowledgeable of the Land Act 1996, Customary Land Registration Act, RSPO rules and regulations and other related laws of PNG
Class 3 drivers Licence desirable.
If you believe that you have the necessary skills and experience, then please send your expression of interest with your CV to:
[email protected]
NLT 02nd March 2026
Apply

Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our supply team, you will assist the Supply & Logistics Manager and Senior Offshore Superintendent with the overall Offsite Materials chain to continually maximise efficiencies whilst minimizing cost to the company & overall material supply chain. In this integral role you will assist with establishing and maintaining close relationships with all external parties being dealt with to ensure timely and seamless process of import and export of materials. You will also ensure the workplace health & safety of employees, contractors and other stakeholders and to minimize the impact of the Supply chain on the environment.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Develop for approval, Implement, and supervise systems and procedures consistent with the Supply Departments governance and policies for proficient management across all functions of the offsite material chain.
Work together with Supply Superintendent, Infield Logistics section, & Managers to plan and execute development of a co-operative operational process and procedures to provide seamless transfers of materials
Manages employees responsible for preparing, staging, and distributing materials as needed to mine site.
Assist with ensuring that KPI goals are met
Adhering to approved budgets and cost transfers within K92 Mining.
Provides input to strategic decisions that affect the functional area of materials responsibility.
Confident in resolving escalated issues arising from operations and requiring coordination with other departments.
Cultivate positive relationships through effective communication and provides constructive feedback to the Supply & Logistics Manager.
Demonstrate commitment to and hold others accountable to complying with the K92 safety management systems and strategies.
Develop succession plans through leading, training and mentoring direct reports to deliver the plan with aim of building a high performing team.
Positively influence and shape the material department culture to ensure a safe, sustainable and disciplined approach to work.
Set weekly and daily priorities for the team, monitor progress and report on activity and outcomes.
Ensure the timely completion of all tasks for both staff and contractors
Liaise with representatives from K92 Mining logistics to ensure that co- operative working relationships are maintained.
Liaise with external parties of Government departments, Contractors, to ensure a positive and seamless process for material imports and exports
Maintain and perform approvals in the Pronto system
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have all or the following
Experience communicating with providers in PNG and internationally
Ability to lead and coach a team with diverse skills
Ability to communicate clearly with people at all levels of the organisation and engage all relevant stakeholders
7 years’ experience in a supervisory role within logistics or materials in mining or similar environment
5 years’ experience of Pronto
Demonstrated problem solving and decision-making capability.
Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly to and influence internal and external stakeholders.
Negotiation skills and understanding of negotiation techniques.

26178.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Advisor Power & Utilities Operations will support operations team in P&U to ensure efficiency and compliance with safety standards.
Essential Duties
Adhere to daily P&U operations
Execute strategies to enhance operational efficiency
Support, collaborate with, and provide assistance to Supervisors P&U Operations
Assess data and report on improvement outcomes
Administer safety protocols and execute regular safety audits
Responsible for assessing relevant risks, executing mitigation measures, and continuously monitoring for risks
Provide technical expertise and support for operational troubleshooting
Produce weekly High-Level Plan (HLP) for execution.
Engauge in weekly planning meetings.
Training & Experience
A commitment to Safety
Relevant academic qualification or trade qualification in Power Generation, Practical knowledge gained from working in relevant Power Station roles - applied knowledge of technical aspects of the role including Power systems, equipment and systems
Practical and applied knowledge of working safely and sustainably in this area of Power generation.
Proven ability to identify risk and taking active steps to mitigate risk
Acquired knowledge of business and process improvement identifying improvement opportunity and taking appropriate action
Competent in safety, health, and sustainability
Knowledge in operation of boiler and steam systems is an advantage.
Knowledge in Heavy Fuel Oil separators operations is an advantage.
Knowledge in Demineralising operation for producing Boiler water is an advantage
Working Conditions
This is a 21/21 FIFO roster.

26177.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Power & Utilities Department at our Lihir operation has an exciting opportunity for a Superintendent – Power & Utilities Mechanical Maintenance. Reporting to the Manager – Power & Utilities, you will lead the mechanical maintenance, planning & reliability, monitoring diagnosis & improving mechanical maintenance work & systems across the various Power & Utilities assets on Lihir Island.
Essential Duties
Lead P&U mechanical maintenance, planning & reliability across all P&U assets, ensuring safety is a top priority & assets are maintained & available to support the site power & steam demands
Develop maintenance procedures and guidelines for effective maintenance of P&U assets in line with site maintenance business practices & systems
Adhere to compliance with safety and environmental regulations
Monitor, Diagnose & Improve teams’ performance & implement improvement strategies
Run budget and resources for power and utilities mechanical maintenance & reliability
Accountable for mechanical reliability across power & utilities assets
Conduct regular inspections and safety audits of power and utilities assets, work & systems
Solve maintenance issues and streamline power and utilities processes
Coach and guide the team on safe work practices & procedures
Responsible for identifying relevant risks, implementing mitigation measures, and continuous risk monitoring
Manage Wartsila Maintenance Contract
Works in established systems and processes
Compares data collected from processes with a known model or system
Extrapolates patterns to make predictions
Improves work methods using significant data and patterns
Training & Experience
A Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, diploma, Mechanical Tradesman or a related field
Several years of experience in power generation systems, mechanical maintenance, and high-pressure steam boilers, demonstrating progression through roles of increasing responsibility
Advanced understanding of power generation & utilities such as reciprocating engine generation, high-pressure steam boilers, potable water plants, demineralization plants, incinerators, safety compliance, and stakeholder collaboration
Advanced knowledge and practical application in maintenance scheduling, performance monitoring, budgeting, risk mitigation and compliance with safety and environmental policies
Competent knowledge of health, safety, environment and sustainability regulations and practices
Competent understanding of project cost management and financial principles
Advanced understanding and application of maintenance systems, SAP, scheduling software programs and tools Competent knowledge of key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics for performance
Competent knowledge of health, safety, environment and sustainability regulations and practices
Competent ability to interact, influence and resolve conflict with various stakeholders
Working Conditions
Roster options include 21:21 or 5:2 on a FIFO or Residential basis.
If you feel that you could make a meaningful contribution in this role, we encourage you to discuss this opportunity with your current people leader and how it aligns with your longer term career goals.
To support you in your application, we have created a range of resources available to all Newmont People including information on eligibility criteria and FAQs. Find out more by visiting our page in Discovery: Internal Employee Resources
As a current employee or contractor, please submit your application is MS Word or Adobe format online via the Internal Job Postings link on Discovery.
If you have issues applying through Discovery or would like to learn more about the role before applying, please contact the relevant member of our Talent Acquisition Team.
Apply

26123.description:
Mine Engineer
Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our Simberi Operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.
We are currently seeking a
Mine Engineer
to join our team. permanent full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 15/13 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Buka, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Wewak, Vanimo or Tabar group of Islands.
(Locals are encouraged to apply)
.
Reporting to the Senior Mine Engineer, the Mine Engineer, is responsible for the preparation of the short term (< 3 Mths) mine engineering and mine planning activities, ensuring Simberi Operations adheres to the site business plans and strategy to realise maximum return for the asset. The role will also provide technical and processional leadership and support to the Simberi Operations, which will be consistent with the Company’s Vision, Values and Policies.
The opportunity
Technical Accountabilities
Mine Planning
Work with the technical services and mining teams to develop short to medium term schedules and forecasts in line with company targets and objectives.
Support the mining operations team to achieve production targets by providing technical support in terms of mine design and planning.
Assist the senior mining engineer in the development and implementation of mine planning and scheduling system, processes, and procedures.
Assist the senior mining engineer with their efforts to ensure that the mine planning team provides a consistently high level of support to mining operations at Simberi.
Coordinate and consult with the mining department and the tech services team to ensure that all the daily mining and planning activities are conducted in a manner which allows safe and efficient mining operations.
Assist with tracking, reporting and analysis of daily, weekly, and monthly mining related production data.
Drill and Blast
Assist with the planning and design of blast holes, tie ups and charging plans as required and provide technical support to the Drill & Blast Team.
Assist with the planning and scheduling of drill and blast operations in line with the short term mine plan and integrate this work with other planning and operational areas.
With the support of the planning team, actively engage with the production team to communicate designs and plans to ensure that the drill & blast processes are optimised.
People Accountabilities
Coordinate resources for the effective delivery of all production planning requirements
Coach, mentor and train the mine engineering team to ensure tasks are consistently completed to a high standard to ensure that mining operations can meet targets and operate efficiently and effectively.
Provide direction and leadership for mining engineers, graduate engineers and others
Are you ready to come and build our future together?
We need the right people. Our vision is to build a high performing mine technical services team to cover all technical mining engineering activities from short term to strategic mine planning, with all work completed on site and minimal reliance on external consultants.
We are looking for people who are highly motivated, have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact.  Additionally, we are looking for people who see a challenge as an opportunity for personal growth and development and value working in a team towards a common goal.
We would love to hear from you if you have:
Essential
Behaviour consistent with St Barbara Values
Ability to produce a PNG National Police Clearance (valid within the last 3 months) for site access purposes
Current unencumbered Papua New Guinea’s ‘C’ Class Driver’s Licence
A degree qualification in mining engineering or related discipline
At least three (3) years’ experience in the mining industry, with appropriate experience in Open Pit mining.
Experienced user of mine design, drill and blast and scheduling software
High level of enthusiasm for the work with high performance goals for self and team
Effective multitasking skills and the ability to work under pressure
Excellent analytical and teamwork skills
Good written and verbal communication skills as well as good organizational and administrative skills.
Desirable
Experience using Deswik software highly desirable.
A Shot Firers permit and Explosive handling certification.
Knowledge of the PNG Mine Safety Act and Regulations
Ability to lead a group of technical professionals

and to apply for this role, please visit:

25736.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Processing Operators are multi skilled technicians responsible for the day-to-day operation of the Process Plant including the
•             Crushing and ore handling system
•             Comminution circuit comprising the SAG and Ball mills and gravity concentrator
•             Flotation circuit
•             Thickening and filtration circuits
•             Concentrate loading
The Processing plant operates on a continuous shift roster operating on both day and night shift.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Perform the day-to-day operation of the process plant including, Crushing and ore handling system, Comminution circuit comprising the SAG and Ball mills and gravity concentrator, Flotation circuit, Thickening and filtration circuits, Concentrate loading, Preparation of reagents
Operate fixed plant equipment according to all K92 Operation & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems.
Effectively operate and maintain equipment mobile plant (light vehicle, front end loader, skid steer loader telehandler) according to all K92 Operation & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems
Monitor equipment and systems to ensure correct and safe operation.
Conduct sampling and monitoring of process plant sections.
Record information and plant operating parameters using logsheets and appropriate documentation.
Assist in isolation and de-isolation of equipment
Perform minor maintenance activities on all equipment and provide input and assistance maintenance personnel as needed.
Perform clean-up and housekeeping to ensure a safe, clean and productive work area.
Conduct machinery inspections throughout to ensure all systems are functioning properly.
Perform daily safety prestart maintenance checks.
Ensure all K92 safety standards, policies & procedures are always adhered to
Ensure that adequate duty of care is exercised in all aspects of work activities.
Ensure utmost compliance of Occupational Health and Safety Regulations and any site-specific rules which may apply.
About You
To be considered for this role, you must have a Grade 10 Certificate and relevant experience as well as Valid PNG Class 3 and Class 6 licence. In addition to this you will have some or all the following.
Machinery licences including loader, skid steer, telehandler (desirable)
Previous experience in a process plant (desirable).
An appropriate trades trade certificate (desirable)
Tertiary qualifications in Mineral Processing are highly desirable.
High risk work certificates including, Working at Heights, Confined Space Entry, Equipment Isolation
Ability to perform duties with minimum supervision.
Ability to work shift work
Able to communicate effectively at all levels, with good written communication skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply
